text:
Maya: Quick q — running a local Docker image with REDWOOD_API_KEY in my env, getting 401 when I set Authorization to Basic <base64>. Docs mention base64 of `api_key:` — is the trailing colon mandatory? Also suspecting Windows path/newline issues with my key.

Jonah: Yes the trailing colon is required. Basic auth encodes username:password, and for API keys the key is the username and password is empty, so you must encode `APIKEY:` (note the colon). Example with curl on mac/linux: `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"APIKEY:\" | base64)\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate`

Lucas: Common gotchas: 1) If your env var contains quotes or a trailing newline (e.g., from copy/paste or from some editors) the base64 changes. Use `echo -n` when testing. 2) .env files: don't wrap the value in extra quotes unless you need them. Wrong: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"sk-xxx\"` — that ends up including the quotes in the value.

Maya: Ah — I'm on Windows dev box and set the key with `setx`. Could that add a newline?

Lucas: setx persists to registry and sometimes introduces issues if you include trailing CRLF when copying. For quick testing in PowerShell do: `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk-xxxx'` (no quotes inside the string). For cmd.exe use `set REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx` in the same shell. If using Docker Desktop with compose, prefer `environment:` with `- REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` or an `env_file:` that has `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` (no quotes).

Jonah: Node examples: header construction must also include the colon. Two short examples — Buffer for Node and fetch: 
```js
// Node (commonjs or modern)
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || ''
const basic = Buffer.from(key + ':').toString('base64')
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Basic ${basic}` } })
```
Or if you prefer bearer tokens (supported on hosted):
```js
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}` } })
```

Jonah: Go example: 
```go
import \"encoding/base64\"
// ...
b := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(apiKey + \":\"))
req.Header.Set(\"Authorization\", \"Basic \"+b)
```

Maya: Is Redwood strictly Basic, or is Bearer acceptable everywhere? I have some libs that default to Bearer.

devex: infra-bot: Redwood hosted supports Bearer as the preferred modern pattern; we also accept Basic for backwards compatibility. For Dedicated/Private setups customers sometimes wire a proxy that expects Basic — check your deployment docs. See: https://internal.redwood/docs/auth#api-keys

Lucas: Also watch CI: some CI secret managers (e.g., GitHub Actions) will mask secrets and may add newlines if you paste with enter. Use the secrets UI paste box. Test locally with `printf '%s' \"$KEY\" | base64` to verify no newline.

Maya: Thanks — fixed it. My mistake was a stray CRLF from a Windows copy. Changed to `$env:...` and now `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$KEY:\" | base64)\"` works. Marking resolved. :tada:

Jonah: Nice! Adding a small note to our devex docs about Windows copy pitfalls.

devex: Loud +1.
